message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine VM that has a single NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
The instructions cover both the **`gcloud` CLI** (the easiest way) and the **REST API** (if you need to embed the call in your own code).

> **Prerequisites**  
> * You have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled.  
> * The **Compute Engine API** is enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).  
> * You have a **GPU quota** for the `nvidia-a6000` accelerator in the zone you choose.  
> * You have the `gcloud` SDK installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).  

---

## 1.  Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables – change these to suit your environment
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports RTX A6000
INSTANCE_NAME="a6000-ubuntu20"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8" # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-a6000"
GPU_COUNT=1
DISK_SIZE_GB=100
DISK_TYPE="pd-ssd"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator=type="$GPU_TYPE",count="$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size="${DISK_SIZE_GB}GB" \
  --boot-disk-type="$DISK_TYPE" \
  --maintenance-policy=TERMINATE \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh
```

### What the command does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the RTX A6000 GPU |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk, 100 GB |
| `--maintenance-policy=TERMINATE` | VM will be terminated (not stopped) during zone maintenance |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restart if the VM crashes |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional startup script (see below) |

#### Optional: GPU driver installation

Google Cloud does **not** pre‑install GPU drivers.  
Add a simple startup script (`startup.sh`) that installs the NVIDIA driver and CUDA toolkit:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Install NVIDIA driver
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535

# Install CUDA (optional, adjust version)
wget https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/cuda-ubuntu2004.pin
sudo mv cuda-ubuntu2004.pin /etc/apt/preferences.d/cuda-repository-pin-600
wget https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/12.2.0/local_installers/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local_12.2.0-535.86.05-1_amd64.deb
sudo dpkg -i cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local_12.2.0-535.86.05-1_amd64.deb
sudo apt-key add /var/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local/7fa2af80.pub
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get -y install cuda

# Reboot to load the driver
sudo reboot
```

> **Tip:** If you only need the driver (no CUDA), you can skip the CUDA section.

---

## 2.  Using the REST API (curl)

If you prefer to embed the call in your own application, use the Compute Engine REST API.  
Below is a `curl` example that posts a JSON payload to create the same instance.

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="a6000-ubuntu20"
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)

# JSON body
read -r -d '' INSTANCE_JSON <<EOF
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\nsudo reboot"
      }
    ]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "maintenancePolicy": "TERMINATE",
  "restartOnFailure": true
}
EOF

# POST request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$INSTANCE_JSON"
```

### Explanation of the JSON fields

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `name` | Instance name |
| `machineType` | Full URL to the machine type |
| `disks[0]` | Boot disk configuration (Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, 100 GB SSD) |
| `networkInterfaces[0]` | Default VPC + external IP |
| `accelerators[0]` | RTX A6000 GPU |
| `metadata.items[0]` | Startup script (installs driver & reboots) |
| `serviceAccounts[0]` | Default service account with full cloud scope |
| `maintenancePolicy` | `TERMINATE` for zone maintenance |
| `restartOnFailure` | Auto‑restart on crash |

> **Note:** The `acceleratorType` URL uses the project‑wide accelerator type.  
> If you’re in a different project, replace `$PROJECT` accordingly.

---

## 3.  Quick sanity check

After the instance is running, you can verify the GPU is visible:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh "$INSTANCE_NAME" --zone="$ZONE" --command="nvidia-smi"
```

You should see a table listing the RTX A6000, its driver version, and usage stats.

---

## 4.  Common pitfalls & troubleshooting

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Quota exceeded** | Request a GPU quota increase in the Cloud Console → IAM & Admin → Quotas. |
| **Instance fails to start** | Check the serial console logs (`gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output`). |
| **Driver not loaded** | Ensure the startup script runs successfully; you may need to add `sleep 30` before reboot. |
| **Zone doesn’t support GPUs** | Verify the zone supports `nvidia-a6000` (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `europe-west4-a`). |

---

### TL;DR

```bash
gcloud compute instances create a6000-ubuntu20 \
  --zone=us-central1-a \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --maintenance-policy=TERMINATE \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh
```

That’s all you need to spin up a GPU‑enabled Ubuntu 20.04 VM on Google Cloud!
